122367.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Sponges have a water transport or canal system Reason: They are generally marine and have a cellular level of organism
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
122367.sol: Sponges have a water transport or canal system. Water enters through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall into a central cavity, spongocoel, from where it goes out through the osculum. This pathway of water transport is helpful in food gathering, respiratory exchange and removal of waste.

122920.subject: Botany
122920.text: Carpel Parts Descriptions A. Stigma 1. Receptive surface for pollen grains B. Style 2. Enlarged basal part of the carpel C. Ovary 3. Elongated tube connecting the ovary to the stigma D. Ovule 4. Attached to the placenta and develops into seeds
122920.sol: The stigma is the receptive surface for pollen grains, the style is the tube connecting the ovary to the stigma, the ovary is the enlarged basal part, and the ovule develops into seeds.

123118.subject: Botany
123118.text: Which of the following flowers represent zygomorphic symmetry?
123118.sol: A flower which can be divided into two equal vertical halves by one plane only is called as zygomorphic, e.g., pea, bean, Cassia and gulmohar. Canna is asymmetrical while mustard, chilly and Datura possess actinomorphic symmetry.

123193.subject: Botany
123193.sol: The family Malvaceae includes 75 genera and 1000 species they are chiefly distributed in tropical and subtropical region of the world. The floral fomula is of malva plant.

123364.subject: Botany
123364.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1.The hypodermis in dicot stems is made of sclerenchymatous cells 2.Vascular bundles in monocot stems are scattered. 3.The pith in dicot stems is composed of collenchymatous cells. 4.Vascular bundles in monocot stems are absent. 5.bundles in monocot stems are arranged in a circle.
123364.sol: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large number of scattered vascular bundles

123441.subject: Botany
123441.text: During secondary growth in dicot stems, the formation of phelloderm from phellogen is an example of which of the following developmental processes?
123441.sol: Phellogen (cork cambium) is a secondary meristem formed by the process of dedifferentiation. When the cells of phellogen divide and the newly formed cells mature to form phelloderm (secondary cortex), they lose their capacity to divide. According to NCERT, the process by which the derivatives of a dedifferentiated tissue lose their ability to divide and mature to perform specific functions is called redifferentiation. Dedifferentiation is incorrect because it refers to the formation of the phellogen itself, not its

123491.subject: Botany
123491.sol: Passage cells are found in monocot root. It is an unthickened cell in the endodermis of a root, found opposite to the protoxylem element through which solutions can diffuse in the transverse direction.

123555.subject: Botany
123555.text: What is the average duration of cell cycle of a human cell?
123555.sol: A typical eukaryotic cell cycle is illustrated by human cells in culture. These cells divide once in approximately every 24 hours. However, this duration of cell cycle can vary from organism to organism and also from cell type to cell type. Yeast for example, can progress through the cell cycle in only about 90 minutes. The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: Interphase, M Phase (Mitosis phase) The M Phase represents the phase when the actual cell division or mitosis occurs and the interphase represents th

123662.subject: Botany
123662.text: What is the first stage of prophase I of meiosis?
123662.sol: Prophase of the first meiotic division is typically longer and more complex when compared to prophase of mitosis. It has been further subdivided into the following five phases based on chromosomal behaviour, i.e., Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis. During leptotene stage the chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope. The compaction of chromosomes continues throughout leptotene. This is followed by the second stage of prophase I called zygotene.

123680.subject: Botany
123680.text: What is the name of the complex structure formed during the zygotene stage of prophase I in meiosis?
123680.sol: During this stage chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis. Such paired chromosomes are called homologous chromosomes. Electron micrographs of this stage indicate that chromosome synapsis is accompanied by the formation of complex structure called synaptonemal complex. The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad. however, these are more clearly visible at the next stage. The first two stages of prophase I are relativel

123707.subject: Botany
123707.text: How do the chromosomes become compact in meiosis II?
123707.sol: Meiosis II is initiated immediately after cytokinesis, usually before the chromosomes have fully elongated. In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis II resembles a normal mitosis. The nuclear membrane disappears by the end of prophase II The chromosomes again become compact. The chromosomes become compact again in meiosis II by elongating, in contrast to meiosis I. Metaphase II: At this stage the chromosomes align at the equator and the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle get attached to the kinetochores of si

123712.subject: Botany
123712.text: What happens to the nuclear envelope during Anaphase II in meiosis?
123712.sol: Prophase II: Meiosis II is initiated immediately after cytokinesis, usually before the chromosomes have fully elongated. In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis II resembles a normal mitosis. The nuclear membrane disappears by the end of prophase II (Figure 10.4). The chromosomes again become compact. Metaphase II: At this stage the chromosomes align at the equator and the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle get attached to the kinetochores (Figure 10.4) of sister chromatids. The nuclear envelope disappears d

124052.subject: Botany
124052.text: What is the structure that connects the central tubules in the axoneme?
124052.sol: The central tubules are connected by bridges and is also enclosed by a central sheath, which is connected to one of the tubules of each peripheral doublets by a radial spoke. Thus, there are nine radial spokes. The peripheral doublets are also interconnected by linkers. Both the cilium and flagellum emerge from centriole-like structure called the basal bodies.

124072.subject: Botany
124072.text: which type of cells are microbodies present?
124072.sol: Many membrane bound minute vesicles called microbodies that contain various enzymes, are present in both plant and animal cells.

124323.subject: Botany
124323.text: Read the following statements regarding the formulation of the cell theory: (I) Matthias Schleiden, a German zoologist, examined a large number of plants and observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells. (II) Theodore Schwann studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer. (III) Schwann also concluded, based on his studies on plant tissues, that the presenc
124323.sol: Statement (I) is incorrect because Matthias Schleiden was a German botanist, not a zoologist. Statement (II) is correct. Theodore Schwann (1839), a British zoologist, reported the presence of a thin outer layer (plasma membrane) in animal cells. Statement (III) is correct. Despite being a zoologist, Schwann studied plant tissues and concluded that the cell wall is a unique character of plant cells. Statement (IV) is correct. Rudolf Virchow (1855) modified the hypothesis of Schleiden and Schwann to give the cell the

124732.subject: Botany
124732.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion and the other is labelled as Reason. Assertion: The decapitated (tip-removed) coleoptile of canary grass continues to bend towards a unilateral light source. Reason: The tip of the coleoptile is the site of production of a transmittable influence that causes the bending of the entire coleoptile. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answe
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
124732.sol: The Assertion is false because the decapitated coleoptile of canary grass fails to bend towards a unilateral light source. Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin observed that the tip of the coleoptile perceives the light stimulus. The Reason is true because they concluded that the tip of the coleoptile is the site of a transmittable influence (later identified as auxin) that causes the bending of the entire coleoptile. When the tip is removed, this influence is absent, and phototropism does not occur. Answer: Assertion

124977.subject: Botany
124977.text: How many molecules of CO2 are produced from the complete oxidation of pyruvate?
124977.sol: For aerobic respiration to take place within the mitochondria, the final product of glycolysis, pyruvate is transported from the cytoplasm into the mitochondria. The crucial events in aerobic respiration are: • The complete oxidation of pyruvate by the stepwise removal of all the hydrogen atoms, leaving three molecules of CO2 . • The passing on of the electrons removed as part of the hydrogen atoms to molecular O2 with simultaneous synthesis of ATP. What is interesting to note is that the first process takes place

125107.subject: Botany
125107.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. In stems, the living cells are organised in thin layers inside and beneath the bark. 2. The cells in the interior are dead and provide only mechanical support. 3. The complete combustion of glucose, which produces CO2 and H2O as end products, yields energy most of which is given out as heat. 4. During the process of respiration, oxygen is utilised, and c
125107.sol: In stems, the living cells are organised in thin layers inside and beneath the bark. The cells in the interior are dead and provide only mechanical support. The complete combustion of glucose, which produces CO2 and H2O as end products, yields energy most of which is given out as heat. During the process of respiration, oxygen is utilised, and carbon dioxide, water and energy are released as products.

125200.subject: Botany
125200.text: Assertion : Conversion of 1,3 biphosphoglycerate (BPGA) to 3-phospho-glyceric acid (PGA) is an energy yielding step. Reason : This energy is trapped in the form of ATP.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
125200.sol: One of the two phosphates of 1,3 biphosphoglycerate (BPGA) is linked by high energy bond. It can synthesise ATP and form 3-phosphoglycerate by phosphoglycerate kinase enzyme. The direct synthesis of ATP from metabolites is called substrate level phosphorylation.

125448.subject: Botany
125448.text: What process do C4 plants lack?
125448.sol: Plants that are adapted to dry tropical regions have the C4 pathway mentioned earlier. Though these plants have the C4 oxaloacetic acid as the first CO2 fixation product they use the C3 pathway or the Calvin cycle as the main biosynthetic pathway. C4 plants are special: They have a special type of leaf anatomy, they tolerate higher temperatures, they show a response to high light intensities, they lack a process called photorespiration and have greater productivity of biomass.

125906.subject: Botany
125906.text: What happens when an animal carrying pollen on its body comes into contact with the stigma?
options: It causes the flower to close
It results in the dispersal of seeds
It leads to the production of nectar
125906.sol: Majority of insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar. When the flowers are small, a number of flowers are clustered into an inflorescence to make them conspicuous. Animals are attracted to flowers by colour and/or fragrance. The flowers pollinated by flies and beetles secrete foul odours to attract these animals. To sustain animal visits, the flowers have to provide rewards to the animals. Nectar and pollen grains are the usual floral rewards. For harvesting the reward(s) from the

125932.subject: Botany
125932.text: What should be done if the female parent plant produces unisexual flowers?
options: The flower buds need to be removed from the plant
The flower buds should be bagged before opening, and pollination is carried out when the stigma is receptive
Pollen from the male parent should be applied directly without any bagging
125932.sol: This is achieved by emasculation and bagging techniques. If the female parent bears bisexual flowers, removal of anthers from the flower bud before the anther dehisces using a pair of forceps is necessary. This step is referred to as emasculation. Emasculated flowers have to be covered with a bag of suitable size, generally made up of butter paper, to prevent contamination of its stigma with unwanted pollen. This process is called bagging. When the stigma of bagged flower attains receptivity, mature pollen grains c

126346.subject: Botany
126346.text: Assertion : The megaspore mother cell undergoes mitosis to produce four megaspores. Reason : Megaspore mother cells and the megaspores are both haploid.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
126346.sol: The diploid megaspore mother cell has a large nucleus and dense cytoplasm. This cell undergoes meiosis (reduction division) to produce a group of four haploid cells called megaspores.

126670.subject: Botany
126670.text: Component Description A. Fatty Acid 1. Glycerol esterified with three fatty acids B. Glycerol 2. Trihydroxy propane C. Phospholipid 3. Contains glycerol, two fatty acids, and a phosphate group D. Nucleotide 4. Contains a nitrogen base, sugar, and phosphate group
126670.sol: Fatty Acid (D) refers to a component that is esterified with glycerol to form fats, like triglycerides (I). Glycerol (B) is a trihydroxy propane (II), a three-carbon alcohol. Phospholipid (C) contains glycerol, two fatty acids, and a phosphate group (III). Nucleotide (A) includes a nitrogen base, sugar, and phosphate group (IV).

126748.subject: Botany
126748.text: Read the following biomolecule-category pairs carefully: (A) Uridine - Nitrogenous base (B) Adenylic acid - Nucleotide (C) Morphine - Alkaloid (D) Carotenoids - Pigment (E) Ricin - Drug How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
126748.sol: Let us evaluate each pair based on the classification of biomolecules: (A) Uridine is a nucleoside (uracil attached to a ribose sugar), not a nitrogenous base. The nitrogenous base itself is uracil. (Incorrect) (B) Adenylic acid has a phosphate group esterified to the sugar of adenosine, making it a nucleotide. (Correct) (C) Morphine is classified as an alkaloid. (Correct) (D) Carotenoids are classified as pigments. (Correct) (E) Ricin is classified as a toxin, whereas drugs include compounds like vinblastin and cu

127615.subject: Botany
127615.text: How many trophic levels are possible in the grazing food chain?
127615.sol: Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called as the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area. The biomass of a species is expressed in terms of fresh or dry weight. Measurement of biomass in terms of dry weight is more accurate. Why?The number of trophic levels in the grazing food chain is restricted as the transfer of energy follows 10 per cent law – only 10 per cent of the energy is transferred to ea

127658.subject: Botany
127658.text: What does the following diagram represent?
127658.sol: The figure represent the inverted biomass pyramid Inverted pyramid of biomass-small standing crop of phytoplankton supports large standing crop of zooplankton

128124.subject: Zoology
128124.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the anatomy of a cockroach. List-I List-II A. Hepatic caeca I. Grinding of food particles B. Malpighian tubules II. Assists in excretion C. Gizzard III. Secretion of digestive juice D. Fat body IV. Excretion of uric acid Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II
A - IV, B - III, C - I, D - II
A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I
A - I, B - II, C - III, D - IV
128124.sol: In a cockroach, Hepatic caeca (or gastric caeca) are a ring of 6-8 blind tubules present at the junction of the foregut and midgut, which secrete digestive juice. Malpighian tubules are a ring of 100-150 yellow-coloured thin filamentous tubules present at the junction of the midgut and hindgut, which help in the removal of excretory products (uric acid). Gizzard (proventriculus) has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plates called teeth, which help in grind

128808.subject: Zoology
128808.text: What happens during a blood transfusion if the blood of a donor is not matched with the blood of a recipient?
options: Blood will be easily accepted by the recipient
Blood will not be easily accepted by the recipient
Blood will be easily rejected by the recipient
128808.sol: ABO grouping is based on the presence or absence of two surface antigens (chemicals that can induce immune response) on the RBCs namely A and B. Similarly, the plasma of different individuals contain two natural antibodies (proteins produced in response to antigens). The distribution of antigens and antibodies in the four groups of blood, A, B, AB and O are given in Table 15.1 . You probably know that during blood transfusion, any blood cannot be used; the blood of a donor has to be carefully matched with the blood

129280.subject: Zoology
129280.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: A nerve impulse is conducted solely by repolarisation Reason: Repolarisation occurs when the inner side of a neuron becomes negatively charged
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
129280.sol: The nerve impulse is conducted along the axon membrane in the form of a wave of depolarisation and repolarisation.

129696.subject: Zoology
129696.text: A patient experiences a significant increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart due to elevated blood volume. Which of the following correctly describes the immediate hormonal response and its direct physiological consequence?
options: Release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF), which stimulates the renin-angiotensin mechanism to maintain glome
Release of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) from the neurohypophysis to further increase blood volume and pressure
Release of aldosterone from the adrenal cortex to promote the excretion of excess sodium and water
Release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF), which causes vasodilation and acts as a check on the renin-angiote
129696.sol: An increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart stimulates the release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF). ANF causes vasodilation (dilation of blood vessels) and thereby decreases blood pressure. Furthermore, ANF acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism, opposing its effects. Option 1 is incorrect because ANF inhibits, rather than stimulates, the renin-angiotensin mechanism. Option 2 is incorrect because ADH is released in response to low blood volume or excessive fluid loss, not elevated blood volum

129731.subject: Zoology
129731.text: Which of the following physiological conditions switches off the osmoreceptors and suppresses the release of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH)?
options: Excessive loss of fluid from the body
A fall in glomerular filtration rate (GFR)
129731.sol: According to NCERT, an increase in body fluid volume switches off the osmoreceptors and suppresses the release of ADH to complete the feedback loop, thereby promoting diuresis. Excessive loss of fluid from the body activates osmoreceptors, stimulating the hypothalamus to release ADH. A fall in GFR or a decrease in blood volume activates the JG cells to release renin (initiating the RAAS pathway) and also stimulates ADH release to conserve water and restore blood pressure. Answer: Increase in body fluid volume

129772.subject: Zoology
129772.sol: Haemodialysis helps the patient suffering from uremia. In this condition, the excretory products (i.e., urea) go on accumulating in blood. This happens due to kidney failure. In haemodialysis the patients blood is passed through disposable dialyser and is then returned to body by the intravenous route.

130050.subject: Zoology
130050.text: A fluid-filled double membranous layer surrounds the lungs. Name it.
130050.sol: A fluid-filled double membranous layer surrounds the lungs and is called Pleura.

130545.subject: Zoology
130545.text: Which age group would benefit the most from proper information about reproductive organs, adolescence, and related changes?
130545.sol: With the help of audio-visual and the print-media governmental and non-governmental agencies have taken various steps to create awareness among the people about reproduction-related aspects. Parents, other close relatives, teachers and friends, also have a major role in the dissemination of the above information. Introduction of sex education in schools should also be encouraged to provide right information to the young so as to discourage children from believing in myths and having misconceptions about sex-related

131214.subject: Zoology
131214.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The placenta acts as an exocrine tissue during pregnancy as it secretes hormones like hCG, hPL, estrogens, and progestogens. Reason (R): The placenta facilitates the supply of oxygen and nutrients to the embryo and also removes carbon dioxide and excretory materials produced by the embryo. In the l
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
131214.sol: The placenta acts as an endocrine tissue (not exocrine) because it secretes hormones such as human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogens, and progestogens directly into the blood. Therefore, the Assertion is incorrect. The placenta also acts as a structural and functional unit between the embryo and the maternal body. It facilitates the supply of oxygen and nutrients to the embryo and removes carbon dioxide and excretory materials produced by the embryo. Therefore, the Reason is co

131837.subject: Zoology
131837.text: During the process of transcription in bacteria, a stage is reached where the nascent RNA falls off and the RNA polymerase also separates from the DNA, marking the end of the process. Which of the following transiently associates with the RNA polymerase to facilitate this specific event?
131837.sol: In prokaryotes, the core RNA polymerase is only capable of catalysing the elongation step of transcription. To terminate the process, the RNA polymerase must transiently associate with a termination factor, known as the (rho) factor, when it reaches the terminator region. This association alters the specificity of the enzyme, causing the nascent RNA and the polymerase to fall off the DNA. The (sigma) factor is required for initiation, not termination. The core enzyme cannot terminate transcription on its own, and D

132266.subject: Zoology
132266.text: What is the likelihood of a heterozygous individual being affected by sickle-cell anaemia?
132266.sol: This is an autosome linked recessive trait that can be transmitted from parents to the offspring when both the partners are carrier for the gene (or heterozygous). The disease is controlled by a single pair of allele, HbA and HbS . Out of the three possible genotypes only homozygous individuals for HbS (HbSHbS ) show the diseased phenotype . Heterozygous (HbAHbS ) individuals appear apparently unaffected but they are carrier of the disease as there is 50 per cent probability of transmission of the mutant gene to th

132884.subject: Zoology
132884.sol: The most important pre-condition for adaptive radiation is a geographic barrier or an isolated habitat.

133044.subject: Zoology
133044.text: When two species of different genealogy come to resemble each other as a result of adaptation, the phenomenon is termed:
133044.sol: The analogous organs show convergent evolution due to similar adaptions which do not support organic evolution. Divergent evolution occurs when two groups of the same species evolve different traits within those groups in order to accommodate for differing environmental and social pressures. Microevolution is the change in allele frequencies that occurs over a relatively short period of time within a population. This change is due to four different processes: mutation, selection, gene flow and genetic drift. Coevol

133375.subject: Zoology
133375.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The most important measure to control diseases like malaria and filariasis is to administer vaccines. Reason: Controlling or eliminating insect vectors and their breeding places is crucial for preventing diseases like malaria and filariasis.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Assertion is false, but Reason is true
133375.sol: For diseases such as malaria and filariasis that are transmitted through insect vectors, the most important measure is to control or eliminate the vectors and their breeding places. This can be achieved by avoiding stagnation of water in and around residential areas, regular cleaning of household coolers, use of mosquito nets, introducing fishes like Gambusia in ponds that feed on mosquito larvae, spraying of insecticides in ditches, drainage areas and swamps, etc. In addition, doors and windows should be provided

133479.subject: Zoology
133479.text: How does the transmission of Amoebiasis take place?
133479.sol: Ingestion of quadrinucleate cysts of Entamoeba histolytica can cause the cysts to be passed from the patient's faeces via food and water.

133488.subject: Zoology
133488.text: A pathological process that is observed in a malignant tumour is known as ____.
133488.sol: A pathological process that is observed in malignant tumours is known as metastasis.

133499.subject: Zoology
133499.text: Which of the following is the reason(s) for Rheumatoid arthritis? Choose the correct option. i. The ability to differentiate pathogens or foreign molecules from self cells increase. ii. The body attacks self cells iii. More antibodies are produced in the body iv. The ability to differentiate pathogens or foreign molecules from self cells is lost
133499.sol: Sometimes, due to genetic and other unknown reasons, the body attacks self-cells. This results in damage to the body and is called auto-immune disease. Rheumatoid arthritis which affects many people in our society is an auto-immune disease.

133517.subject: Zoology
133517.text: A patient presents with symptoms of fatigue, weakening, and paralysis of skeletal muscles. Clinical investigations reveal that the patient's own immune system is producing antibodies that attack the neuromuscular junction. Identify the disease and its correct biological categorization.
133517.sol: The symptoms described (fatigue, weakening, and paralysis of skeletal muscles) and the specific targeting of the neuromuscular junction are characteristic of Myasthenia gravis. Because the patient's own immune system produces antibodies against their own receptors, it is classified as an autoimmune disorder. Muscular dystrophy is a genetic disorder that causes progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle, not an autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction. Answer: Myasthenia gravis - Autoimmune disorder

133789.subject: Zoology
133789.text: Why is the use of insecticides and pesticides harmful to human beings and animals?
options: They are toxic and extremely harmful
They are not as harmful as natural methods
133789.sol: Biocontrol refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests. In modern society, these problems have been tackled increasingly by the use of chemicals – by use of insecticides and pesticides. These chemicals are toxic and extremely harmful, to human beings and animals alike, and have been polluting our environment (soil, ground water), fruits, vegetables and crop plants. Our soil is also polluted through our use of weedicides to remove weeds.

133974.subject: Zoology
133974.text: Which of the following microorganisms is employed for the commercial production of acetic acid?
133974.sol: Acetobacter aceti is a bacterium used for the commercial production of acetic acid. Aspergillus niger is a fungus that produces citric acid. Clostridium butylicum is a bacterium that produces butyric acid. Lactobacillus is a bacterium that produces lactic acid. Answer: Acetobacter aceti

134816.subject: Zoology

134979.subject: Zoology
134979.text: A foreign DNA and plasmid cut by the same restriction endonuclease can be joined to form a recombinant plasmid using
134979.sol: In DNA recombinant technology, linking of foreign DNA and the plasmid is made possible by DNA ligase which is also called "molecular glue".

135320.subject: Zoology
135320.text: Which of the following would necessarily decrease the density of a population in a given habitat?
135320.sol: Mortality and emigration would necessarily decrease the density of a population in a given habitat.

96489.sol: Ecological succession is a predictable process; therefore, it can be predicted which stage will come before or after any stage. 96515.subject: Botany
96515.text: For an ecosystem, the two main structural features are - (i) Species composition (ii) Energy flow (iii) Decomposition (iv) Stratification
96515.sol: The basic structural and functional unit of ecology is an ecosystem which is made up of abiotic and biotic components. There is a characteristic physical structure within each ecosystem due to the interaction of abiotic and biotic components. Species composition and stratification form the two main structural features of an ecosystem. For any ecosystem to function and sustain, solar energy supply is a basic requirement.

96612.subject: Botany
96612.text: The trophic level of zooplankton living in an aquatic ecosystem will be:
96612.sol: The step or position in a nutritive series like food chain is referred to as trophic level. There are different trophic levels in an ecosystem and food chain. The producers (photosynthetic organisms) form the first trophic level. The phytoplanktons form the first trophic level T 1 in an aquatic system and the zooplanktons form the second trophic level ( T 2 ) as they are the consumers that feed on producers.
